Q: CkEditor5 insertContent Function not working A:

On top of danwellman's answer, you might have to enable all the possible incoming html elements, and also enable plugin "GeneralHtmlSupport"

plugins: [ GeneralHtmlSupport, /* ... */ ],
htmlSupport: {
    allow: [
      // We need to allow this for every element that possibly gets injected
      { name: 'span', attributes: true, classes: true, styles: true },
      { name: 'table', attributes: true, classes: true, styles: true },
      { name: 'tr', attributes: true, classes: true, styles: true },
      { name: 'th', attributes: true, classes: true, styles: true },
      { name: 'td', attributes: true, classes: true, styles: true },
      { name: 'thead', attributes: true, classes: true, styles: true },
      { name: 'tbody', attributes: true, classes: true, styles: true },
      { name: 'ul', attributes: true, classes: true, styles: true },
      { name: 'ol', attributes: true, classes: true, styles: true },
      { name: 'li', attributes: true, classes: true, styles: true },
    ],
  },
},

And then to insert:

let html = `<span class="some" styles="color:red;">`
const viewFragment = editor.data.processor.toView(html)
const modelFragment = editor.data.toModel(viewFragment)
// Insert where the cursor is
editor.model.insertContent(modelFragment, editor.model.document.selection)

Notice!

  • <span>'s will still get wrapped in a <p> tag

  • <p> tags will NOT get wrapped

  • <div>'s are by default always converted to <p> tags, even if you put them in the "allow" section. you might need another workaround for that.

Q: Why do I get "ERROR ITMS-90296: App sandbox not enabled" when I upload the PKG file via Application Loader? A:

For your second problem you need to make an entitlements.plist file and add com.apple.security.app-sandbox and other entitlements you need.

There are more problems to be solved e.g. codesigning, extracting dylibs, placing provisionprofiles at the right places. Read more: Guide to publishing a Java app to the Mac App Store. I've made Java Electron as example. This includes a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes to TestFlight. The showcase app that has passed the Apple App Store review process successfully is Backdoor, a modern database tool for querying and editing data.

Q: How can I solve the "unhashable type" error when importing TensorFlow in Python? A:

Welcome to Python dependency-management hell.

I'm not sure there is any easy or short answer to your question. What you're stumbling onto is a very common issue in any Pythonista's journey.

The libs you're using on one computer appear to be aligned with each other, while on the other, they're not (having a lib complaining about another during its import is a good sign of a dependencies issue). And it's going to be impossible to make sure they're all ok in all contexts within a single environment.

The way we usually solve this in the Python community is by using a dependency manager.

Here is the Real Python article about dependency management and why you need it. It's a long read, but well worth it.

Good luck!
